text:
Elaine: Quick sync — we need to lock down the audit event tombstone & versioning approach for customer-facing events before next Wed's Dedicated GA. High-level proposal: add a top-level "event_version" (int), introduce a per-field "tombstone" marker in the schema, and do soft-coexistence for 90 days. Also need a migration checklist for customer validators. Thoughts?

Tyler: +1 on soft-coexistence. Prefer we avoid removing fields from the wire until we've run customer validators and given notice. Suggest we also add a server-side flag so we can stop emitting deprecated fields without breaking consumers who still expect them.

Maria: KMS note — some of the new fields carry key identifiers (key_id). With key rotation we can end up with multiple identifiers pointing to the same material. Can we standardize on key_fingerprint (sha256) in events instead of raw key IDs? That will help customer validators and deduping. Also needs docs for how KMS rotations affect audit immutability.

Jon: Question on versioning scope: per-event-type version vs global audit stream version. My vote is per-event-type (e.g., user.created v2) so consumers can upgrade incrementally. Global stream forces every consumer to understand all event types.

Elaine: Agreed with Jon. Plan: event_version at the root plus event_type string. Example payload proposal:```json
{
  "event_type": "access_grant",
  "event_version": 2,
  "timestamp": "2026-03-22T18:03:00Z",
  "actor": { "id": "usr_123", "role": "admin" },
  "details": { "resource": "model:ada-1", "action": "grant" },
  "deprecated_fields": ["legacy_key_id"],
  "kms_key_fingerprint": "sha256:abcdef..."
}
```
(we're using lowercase snake/camel consistency TBD in schema doc)

Tyler: That sample looks good. Two follow-ups: 1) how do we express field-level tombstones for nested fields (details.resource.old_name)? 2) what telemetry will alert us if customer validators fail?

Maria: For nested fields I propose we use dotpath strings in "deprecated_fields" (e.g., "details.resource.old_name"). For validators: we should publish a validation webhook that customers can run against their proxy, plus an internal validator that runs on canary traffic and posts diffs to the security audit dashboard.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: canary policy will run v2 validator on 2% of traffic for 48h after rollout. Link: https://console.redwood.ai/canaries/validator-v2

Elaine: Action items before EOD Fri:
- Tyler to draft migration playbook + server-side emit-flag (ETA Fri)
- Maria to update KMS guidance and agree fingerprint format (ETA Thu)
- Jon to implement validator checks + webhook prototype (ETA Mon)
- Security to prepare customer-facing notice + exampless

Tyler: I'll add a feature flag (audit-v2-coexist) and a short runbook for rollback. We should also add a metric count.audit.deprecated_field_emitted and an alert if >1% traffic emits a deprecated field after the 90-day soft window.

Maria: For customer notice, recommend a phased timeline: notice (30d), validator window (30d), emit-stop soft-deprecation (90d), hard-remove (120d). Needs legal + support signoff.

Jon: I'll spin up the validator lambda and post a test harness link. Also will add an opt-in customer sample program to help the largest consumers run validation.

Elaine: OK — will summarize and open the RFC doc. Thanks all. :white_check_mark: 

(threads/notes: keep event_version integer, document backward compatibility rules, ensure KMS fingerprinting is reversible for audit purposes, coordinate with support for the customer notice cadence.)
